settings.label: Measurement ID
settings.meaning: The web data stream the page tag and the server's events report to. It is G- followed by capital letters and digits, and it is not a secret: the page tag puts it in every page.
settings.whereToFind: Admin › Data collection and modification › Data streams › your web stream: Measurement ID. Google Analytics has no test mode: use a separate property (or at least a separate stream) for test.

settings.label: Measurement Protocol API secret
settings.meaning: Lets the server send events to the stream (the Measurement Protocol). Leave it unset if the app only uses the page tag or reports.
settings.whereToFind: Admin › Data streams › your web stream › Measurement Protocol API secrets › Create. Google says to rotate it regularly.

settings.label: Property ID
settings.meaning: The property reports are read from (the Data API): a number, not the G- measurement ID. Only needed for reports.
settings.whereToFind: Admin › Property settings › Property details: Property ID, a number such as 123456789.

settings.label: Service account key
settings.meaning: A Google Cloud service account's key file, as JSON. It signs the requests that read reports. Only needed for reports.
settings.whereToFind: Google Cloud console › IAM & Admin › Service accounts › your service account › Keys › Add key › JSON; the whole downloaded file is the value. Enable the Google Analytics Data API in the same Cloud project, and add the service account's email as a Viewer under Google Analytics Admin › Property access management.

settings.label: Collection region
settings.meaning: Set to eu to send the server's events to Google's EU collection endpoint (region1.google-analytics.com). Leave it unset otherwise.

operations.name: events.send
operations.purpose: Sends up to 25 events from the server for one browser (its client_id from the _ga cookie): POST /mp/collect?measurement_id=…&api_secret=… with { client_id, user_id?, timestamp_micros?, user_properties?, consent?, events: [{ name, params }] }. With region eu the host is region1.google-analytics.com. It answers 2xx whenever the request arrives, even when the events are invalid and dropped: only events.validate checks them.

operations.name: events.validate
operations.purpose: Checks events without recording them: the same request as events.send, at /debug/mp/collect, with validation_behavior ENFORCE_RECOMMENDATIONS. Answers { validationMessages: [{ fieldPath, description, validationCode }] }, empty when the events are valid. It doesn't check the API secret or the measurement ID.

operations.name: reports.run
operations.purpose: Runs a report on the property's event data: POST https://analyticsdata.googleapis.com/v1beta/properties/{propertyId}:runReport with { dimensions, metrics, dateRanges, limit, offset, orderBys }, authorized with the service account's access token (scope analytics.readonly).

operations.name: reports.runRealtime
operations.purpose: Runs a report on the last 30 minutes of events: POST https://analyticsdata.googleapis.com/v1beta/properties/{propertyId}:runRealtimeReport with { dimensions, metrics, limit, orderBys, minuteRanges }, authorized like reports.run.

operations.name: serviceAccount.token
operations.purpose: Exchanges a JWT signed with the service account's key (RS256; iss its client_email, scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/analytics.readonly, aud https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token, exp at most an hour after iat) for an access token: POST https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token, form grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer and assertion. The token is reused until shortly before it expires.
